title: Let Not the Wise Their Wisdom Boast
description: Let Not the Wise Their Wisdom Boast in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 650 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Glorying in Christ”, where the book credits them to Wesley's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let not the wise their wis-dom boast; The might-y glo-ry in his might; The rich in flat-tering rich-es trust, Which take their ev-er-last-ing flight.

lines: Let not the wise their wisdom boast;
The mighty glory in his might;
The rich in flattering riches trust,
The rush of numerous years bears down
The most gigantic strength of man;
And where is all his wisdom gone,
When dust he turns to dust again?
The Lord, my righteousness, I praise,
I triumph in the love divine,
The wisdom, wealth, and strength of grace
In Christ through endless ages mine.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
